paragraphs.text: Marvel's Spider-Man (stylized as Magic: The Gathering —Marvel's Spider-Man ) is a tentpole set in the Magic: The Gathering Universes Beyond series released by Wizards of the Coast in collaboration with Marvel Entertainment . The set was released on September 26, 2025. Marvel's Spider-Man is Standard legal and can be counted as the 107th Magic expansion. The set was designed with Pick-Two Draft (4-player draft) in mind. Spider typal and the web-slinging mechanic represent Spider-Man's heroics, while Villain typal and the mayhem and connive mechanics represent Spider-Man's adversaries.

The main Standard-legal set uses the code SPM and features 193 regular cards (65 commons, 55 uncommons, 53 rares, 15 mythic rares, 5 basic lands) . Alternate card frames have a different card number than the original version.
↑ Spectacular Spider-Man is borderless in its default form as well as all of its variants.
The related non-Standard code is SPE; these cards are legal in eternal-legal formats like Commander , Legacy , and Vintage .
Marvel's Spider-Man features Marvel Source Material cards. These may be found in Play Boosters and may be played in Limited games.

Marvel's Spider-Man was sold in Play Boosters , Collector Boosters , the Spider-Man Bundle , a Scene Box and five welcome decks . Unusually, it did not feature any preconstructed Commander decks . The main set features 198 regular cards (65 commons, 55 uncommons, 53 rares, 15 mythic rares, 10 basic lands) , and includes randomly inserted traditional foil versions of all cards.
A year after the Marvel's Spider-Man release, the Spider-Mania Commander deck was part of the Marvel Super Heroes Holiday Release on December 4, 2027.

Each Play Booster contains 14 cards: 6–7 commons, 3 uncommons, 1 rare or mythic rare, 1 wildcard slot with a card of any rarity, 1 traditional-foil card of any rarity, and 1 land, all from the main set. Panel and web-slinger cards can be found in any slot except the common, uncommon, and land slots; scene cards can be found in the same slots and in the uncommon slot. One in every 24 boosters includes a borderless source material card from the bonus sheet, replacing the seventh common slot. Each booster also contains a non-foil double-sided token. A Play Booster box contains 30 packs.

Each Collector Booster contains 15 cards: 5 traditional foil commons, 4 traditional foil uncommons (which can include scene cards), 1 traditional foil spiderweb basic land, 1 traditional foil default frame rare or mythic rare, 2 non-foil alternate-frame rare or mythic rare cards, 1 borderless source material card from the bonus sheet, and 1 foil alternate-frame rare or mythic rare. All slots except the last two can contain SPE cards. Several card treatments are exclusive to Collector Boosters: extended art cards, classic comic cards, textured foil costume change cards, and the Gauntlet and textless cosmic versions of The Soul Stone. A Collector Booster box contains 12 packs.

The Source Material bonus sheet is a collection of additional cards released alongside the main set. It contains reprinted cards themed for Spider-Man with iconic art from Marvel's comic book artists. Play Boosters may contain one of these forty cards with the MAR expansion code. Collector Boosters are guaranteed to contain one MAR card.
Marvel's Spider-Man features five Welcome Decks .

The set includes borderless scene cards. When brought together, these cards form a scene from the books (Spider-Man Showcase Scene; SPM #199-207). These can be found in both Play Boosters and Collector Boosters .

A separately sold Scene Box includes six additional borderless scene cards with the SPE expansion code (Spidey's Spectacular Showdown; SPE #21–26). The box also includes three Play Boosters, six art cards , and a display easel.
Marvel's Spider-Man includes seven tokens.
Copy for Impostor Syndrome .
3/3 Illusion Villain creature for Mysterio, Master of Illusion .
2/1 Spider creature with reach for Origin of Spider-Man , Peter Parker , Spiders-Man, Heroic Horde and Wall Crawl .
1/1 Human Citizen creature for Friendly Neighborhood , News Helicopter , Silk, Web Weaver and Spider-Girl, Legacy Hero .
Food artifact for City Pigeon , Hot Dog Cart and Spider-Ham, Peter Porker .
1/1 Robot artifact creature with flying for Robotics Mastery and Spider-Slayer, Hatred Honed .
Treasure artifact for Common Crook , J. Jonah Jameson , Pictures of Spider-Man , Professional Wrestler and Ultimate Green Goblin .

As part of Spider-Man's repertoire of abilities, the set introduces the Web-slinging keyword ability . It is an alternative cost for spells which includes returning a tapped creature you control to its owner's hand.

Two keywords represent the schemes of Spider-Man's rogues' gallery. The first, returning from Streets of New Capenna , is Connive . When a creature connives, its controller draws a card, discards a card, and then puts a +1/+1 counter on that creature if the discarded card was nonland. This synergizes with the second ability, Mayhem , a retooled version of madness . If a spell has a mayhem cost, it can be cast for that cost from a graveyard if it was discarded this turn. Unlike with madness, it doesn't have to be cast immediately.
Another returning concept is Modified , a batching term that collectively refers to creatures that are equipped , enchanted , or have counters on them.

There are multiple double-faced cards in the set, representing the characters and their secret identities. With cards like Peter Parker // Amazing Spider-Man , it features the first modal double-faced cards that can transform .
To make Limited formats smoother, the set heavily features hybrid mana . Hybrid appears on cards of all rarities.
As a one-off on The Soul Stone , the set introduces the harness ability and the ∞ ( infinity ) ability.
Spider-Man introduces the Symbiote card type. Villain is reintroduced as an eternal type. Both Villain and Hero have mechanical relevance.

Human characters whose genetic codes contain animal DNA are given a corresponding creature type (e.g., Spider ). When the first cards were revealed, a controversy arose around the fact that the Green Goblin was being typed as a Goblin , even though goblins as such don't exist in the Marvel Universe. With the set's focus specifically on Spider-Man, Spider typal is a theme of the set.
The set also adds the Infinity and Stone artifact types , which - unlike Time Lord before it - was made two separate types.
Sand is used for the first time on the type line of a non-token card.
The set has a significant number of common legendary creatures due to its smaller size and the vast array of characters across the Spider-Verse .
Pumpkin Bombs makes use of fuse counters , which haven't been used since Odyssey . The set also reuses ingenuity counters and introduces film counters .
As a set designed for Pick-Two Draft , Marvel's Spider-Man features five limited archetypes (two-color allied).
: Connive and Villain typal
: Mayhem and " discard matters"
: "Mana value 4+ matters"
: Web-slinging and ETB / LTB effects

This is a crossover product based on the Marvel Universe , a fictional shared universe where the stories in most American comic book titles and other media published by Marvel Comics take place. It is notably based on the original comics and not on the Marvel Cinematic Universe . Peter Parker is a full-time superhero better known as the web-slinging and wall-crawling Spider-Man. As an orphaned child, Peter was raised by his Uncle Ben and Aunt May. At a science expo, Peter was bitten by an errant radioactive spider , which granted him an array of arachnid powers. Spider-Man features characters and stories from across its comic history. This includes characters from the extended Spider-Verse ].

Marvel's Spider-Man is the first major release in a series of products created for Magic: The Gathering by Hasbro ( Wizards of the Coast ) in collaboration with Marvel Entertainment . It is themed around the superhero Spider-Man . Among R&D , there was a consciousness that Spider-Man had a potential to bring in a higher volume of new players versus other Universes Beyond properties, but the set was designed as an expert set and not an introductory set, albeit one leaning towards the less complex side. It was designed specifically with the new Pick-Two Draft format in mind.

This set is roughly 80 cards smaller than a usual Standard set. At the start of design, it was going to be an even smaller set. The idea initially was that the set would be legal in all formats and focused on Commander . It would consist of this 100 cards without commons, which was similar to the Assassin's Creed Beyond Booster set. One of those reasons to make the set larger was that the smaller size was forcing R&D to cut a lot of characters and other elements they wanted to include. Another reason was that they had gotten feedback that players were less satisfied with smaller set sizes.

Previously, a modal double-faced card couldn't transform , but that rule is removed. Any modal double-faced permanent that is instructed to transform now can. For the terminology, this means that transforming double-faced card ( TDFC ) is replaced by nonmodal double-faced cards ( NDFC ).

Starting with Marvel's Spider-Man , Universes Beyond cards no longer have the inverted triangle replacing the standard oval security stamp for rare and mythic rare cards, nor the triangular stamp printed in silver on common and uncommon Universes Beyond cards. The special Universes Beyond card frame is also retired. After this change, UB cards can still be recognized by the additional copyright notifications for the used IPs.
In addition, this set introduces character-specific pronouns on the rules text of legendary creature cards in Universes Beyond sets. R&D already included these on Secret Lair cards in the past.

The set is included in the yearlong Marvel Super Heroes VS Villains consumer products campaign. This also includes Marvel Legends action figures with exclusive Magic prom cards. The set is accompanied by the Secret Lair Drop Series: Marvel's Spider-Man Superdrop .
The Headliner for this set is The Soul Stone . The textless cosmic foil version of this card can be found only in Collector Boosters.

Magic Presents: A Villainous Halloween: October 31–November 2, 2025. A special Commander event. Players bring their own Commander decks and, at the start of the game, secretly choose a villain card, each representing a classic villain from Magic’s history with its own alternate win condition. As the game unfolds, players can work toward their secret objective. Once a player meets the condition on their chosen villain card, they reveal it — and from that point on, each opponent loses the game at the end of their own turn, unless they can stop the villain in time.

Following spoiler season, Marvel's Spider-Man was given negative reviews by Tolarian Community College and by Saffron Olive of MTGGoldfish . Both criticized the large number of Spider-Man variants with similar names , the lack of support for traditional eight-player Draft , the non-fantastical depictions of New York City on some cards, and the Through the Omenpaths digital treatment. Tolarian Community College characterized the set as "muddy, clunky, and incoherent" and a failure of crossover game design, cluttered by "minor characters and obscure story beats". SaffronOlive called it " parasitic ", criticizing the lack of backwards compatibility with existing Spider- typal strategies.

Limited Resources prematurely ended their coverage of Marvel's Spider-Man less than a week after release, criticizing the quality of its Draft format and the Through the Omenpaths digital treatment. Co-host Luis Scott-Vargas also noted low engagement with his and other creators' Marvel's Spider-Man and Through the Omenpaths content, claiming to have "never seen a set with less interest" other than March of the Machine: The Aftermath . Writing for Card Kingdom , Jacob Lackner of Nizzahon Magic gave the set an "F" when ranking 2025's limited formats, calling it "one of the worst Limited formats of all time, right there with Coldsnap ". In addition to the small size of the set making cards appear too often, he criticized the color imbalance of the set, calling red "unplayable", a sentiment echoed by Limited Resources .

On October 15, Wizards of the Coast released a feedback survey for the set as normal. Some survey-takers were asked, "To what degree did negative influencer commentary impact your perception of Magic: The Gathering | Marvel's Spider-Man before the set released?" The question was controversial in the community, as some players felt that Wizards of the Coast was shifting responsibility for the set's reception onto content creators. Blake Rasmussen responded to the backlash, calling the question's focus on negative commentary "unusual and not great" while stating that the results would not be used to punish creators or to change Wizards' creator strategy.
As of March 2026, Marvel's Spider-Man is one of Magic 's top ten best-selling sets.

In April 2025, Wizards of the Coast initially announced that Marvel's Spider-Man would not be receiving a release on their digital platforms, Magic Online and Magic: The Gathering Arena . Instead, a mechanically identical set re-themed with Magic in-universe creative treatments, art, and card names was released under the banner of Through the Omenpaths . These Through the Omenpaths cards are legal in all formats that would otherwise have used Marvel's Spider-Man but did not have any physical copies printed at the time of their release.
paragraphs.section: Through the Omenpaths and eventual digital release

paragraphs.text: In a surprise announcement made roughly one month before the release on the next Marvel set, Marvel Super Heroes , Wizards of the Coast announced that they had not only secured the ability to add future Marvel sets to their digital clients, but also that Marvel's Spider-Man would be released retroactively on June 16, 2026 on both Magic Online and MTG Arena under this new agreement. Marvel's Spider-Man became the "default" version of the set sold on both Magic Online and MTG Arena . However, in order to allow players to play with whatever versions of the cards they like the most, both clients kept the Through the Omenpaths versions available in some capacity.
paragraphs.section: Through the Omenpaths and eventual digital release

paragraphs.text: On Magic Online , the Through the Omenpaths versions continue to exist as distinct card objects and are treated as equivalent to their Spider-Man counterparts for gameplay and deckbuilding purposes. Sales of Through the Omenpaths booster packs through the Magic Online store ceased and were replaced by Marvel's Spider-Man Play and Premium Boosters.
paragraphs.section: Through the Omenpaths and eventual digital release

paragraphs.text: MTG Arena converted all Through the Omenpaths printings to card styles upon the release of Marvel's Spider-Man , with players gaining the corresponding Marvel's Spider-Man card in their collection as a replacement. All Through the Omenpaths boosters in a player's collection were automatically opened and their contents converted into Marvel's Spider-Man cards as part of this process. Cards from the Through the Omenpaths Bonus sheet remain as their own separate printings and were not converted to card styles. Sales of Through the Omenpaths booster packs in the store ceased and were replaced by Marvel's Spider-Man boosters.
